messages:
nina_customer: Hi team — we've been seeing intermittent p95/p99 spikes and a few 429s for tenant=brightbeam on Dedicated EU-WEST-1 pool (pool-id: euw-ded-42). Started ~2026-03-12 09:05 UTC. Baseline latency fine, spikes are sudden and correlate with tenant bursts. Any quick triage steps?
elaine_support: Thanks @nina_customer — sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the tenant id, example request timestamps, and whether this is hitting a specific model or route? Also which dedicated pool (exact name/id) so we can check node packing.
nina_customer: tenant=brightbeam, pool=euw-ded-42, model=gptx-13b-std, spike window sample: 2026-03-12T09:05:27Z -> 09:06:10Z. p95 normally ~80ms, observed ~320ms; p99 up to 2.3s. 429s ~0.7% of requests in that window. This only affects requests routed to euw-ded-42.
elaine_support: Got it. Can you run a quick repro (if safe) — a few low-concurrency short prompt calls — and paste the curl you use? Also enable debug-trace header X-RDWD-TRACE=1 so we capture runtime IDs.
nina_customer: Repro curl below (short prompt, synchronous):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.company/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "X-RDWD-TRACE: 1" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-13b-std","input":"Summarize: quick test","max_tokens":32}'
```

We can produce logs for 09:05:20 -> 09:07:00 if you tell me exact trace IDs to look for.
sam_eng_oncall: Jumping in. Please paste the X-RDWD-TRACE values when you repro. In the meantime I'll look at the pool packing and MIG slices. Quick ask: roughly what qps/burst size does brightbeam send? Are they mostly 1-3 token responses (so many tiny calls) or longer streaming?
nina_customer: Bursts are small synchronous calls: 30-50 reqs/s for ~20s bursts. Responses are short (20-60 tokens). No streaming used.
mike_infra: i've checked node host-euw-12 (one of the nodes serving euw-ded-42) around that time. Observations: co-resident tenants packed on fractional MIG slices. During the burst the SM util peaked ~98%, L3 cache miss rate up ~3-4x baseline, and KV cache eviction metric showed lockstep thrash. Snippet of collected metrics: 

```
host: host-euw-12
node_mig: 1g.5gb-slice-0x3
sm_util_pct: 98 -> avg 12
l3_miss_rate: 0.9% -> 3.8%
kv_cache_evictions/s: 120 -> 980
runtime_retries: 0 -> 4
```

Hypothesis: fractional MIG packing + aggressive autoscaler/downscale churn leads to tenant A and tenant B being colocated on same MIG partition. Short, synchronous bursts from tenant A are causing KV cache eviction and SM thrash that impacts tenant B (brightbeam) causing p95 spikes and occasional 429s.
elaine_support: That matches a noisy-neighbor pattern. Two immediate triage/mitigation steps you can try: 1) temporarily set brightbeam to pack-avoid label so scheduler won't pack them on fractional slices, 2) increase dedicated pool min-replicas to reduce pack/unpack churn during bursts, or 3) migrate brightbeam off the currently noisy node (we can remote-evict their instances). Commands: 

```
# add pack-avoid label to tenant
rdwdctl tenants update brightbeam --labels pack=avoid

# drain node (infra action)
kubectl cordon host-euw-12 && kubectl drain host-euw-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n redwood-runtime

# bump pool min replicas (console or API)
curl -X PATCH https://internal-api.redwood.company/v1/pools/euw-ded-42 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"min_replicas":3}'
```

These are temporary mitigations while we root cause.
nina_customer: Will pack-avoid cause any downtime? And how will billing be affected if we increase min_replicas?
sam_eng_oncall: pack-avoid is soft — scheduler will prefer not to colocate but won't evict existing pods immediately. No downtime expected for new allocations; existing ones keep running. Bumping min_replicas will increase reserved capacity costs for that pool tier (pro-rated). We can do a timed migration window with minimal customer impact.
mike_infra: Additional note on root cause — autoscaler aggressively scales to zero for idle slots then back up for bursts. That scale-down/up leads to fractional packing decisions that surface this interference. Long-term fix options: avoid fractional MIG mixing for high-burst latency-sensitive tenants (pin whole MIG slices), improve KV cache isolation (per-tenant namespaces), or make autoscaler prefer node-level isolation for flagged tenants.
elaine_support: For immediate diagnosis can you run these two runtime probes and paste outputs: 1) runtime kv cache status, 2) nvidia dmon for SM occupancy over 60s window. Commands: 

```
# kv cache stats (on runtime pod)
kubectl exec -n redwood-runtime runtime-pod-abc -- /bin/sh -c "rdwd-runtime inspect kvcache --tenant brightbeam"

# gpu dmon (on host)
ssh infra@host-euw-12 "nvidia-smi dmon -s mu -d 1 -c 60"
```

Please paste outputs; i'll correlate with our traces.
nina_customer: pasted below (sanitized):

```
KVCache: tenant=brightbeam
entries_total: 42k
entries_active: 3.2k
evictions_60s: 980
avg_hit_rate: 12%

nvidia dmon sample (sm_pct): 95, 92, 98, 97, 96, 94 (60s window)
```

Looks like eviction and sm saturation lines up with p95 spikes.
sam_eng_oncall: confirmed. Given that we see high kv evictions and SM saturation, this is noisy neighbor. I'll open an infra ticket to migrate brightbeam off host-euw-12 and to schedule a controlled repack with pack-avoid labels. Reasonable next steps: 1) infra will cordon+drain host-euw-12 for the impacted pods, 2) apply pack-avoid for brightbeam for 48h, 3) increase pool min_replicas until we implement per-tenant MIG pinning.

mike_infra: filed INFRA-2026-842. I'll kick off the migration during a quiet window in ~15m unless you prefer sooner. Non-disruptive but expect a few warmup latencies while new instances get KV warmed.
deploy-bot: INFRA-2026-842 scheduled: migrate brightbeam off host-euw-12 in 10 minutes. Notifying oncall.
nina_customer: Thanks all — please include expected window for warmup and any billing delta. I'll monitor and report back if spikes persist.
elaine_support: We'll keep this thread updated. If spikes persist after migration we will experiment with model-variant fallbacks (e.g., route to gptx-13b-q4 for low-latency bursts) and consider longer-term isolation. :thumbsup:
